import sys
from collections import deque

SPOT_VALUE = {1: 20, 2: 60, 3: 140}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Init
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
line = input().split()
MAP_SIZE = int(line[0])
MY_ID = int(line[1])

spot_count = int(input())
known_spots = {}
for _ in range(spot_count):
    parts = input().split()
    sx, sy, stype = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]), int(parts[2])
    max_e = SPOT_VALUE.get(stype, 10)
    known_spots[(sx, sy)] = (stype, max_e)

turn = 0

def neighbors(x, y):
    for dy in range(-1, 2):
        for dx in range(-1, 2):
            if dx == 0 and dy == 0:
                continue
            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
            if 0 <= nx < MAP_SIZE and 0 <= ny < MAP_SIZE:
                yield nx, ny

def count_neighbors(x, y, cell_set):
    return sum(1 for nx, ny in neighbors(x, y) if (nx, ny) in cell_set)

def bfs_next_step(my_cells_set, opp_cells_set, target_x, target_y):
    """BFS outward from the target over the fixed (never mutated) my_cells_set; the
    first frontier node touching it is adjacent to that owned cell and one step
    closer to the target - the single most efficient hop toward it this turn.
    Routes around opponent cells instead of searching through them: without this,
    if the shortest path to a target happens to run through enemy territory, this
    would keep returning that same blocked cell turn after turn (EXPAND onto an
    enemy cell is invalid, so the action is silently dropped), leaving the bot
    sitting on full energy with nothing to do instead of finding a way around."""
    if (target_x, target_y) in my_cells_set:
        return None
    visited = {(target_x, target_y)}
    queue = deque([(target_x, target_y)])
    while queue:
        cx, cy = queue.popleft()
        for nx, ny in neighbors(cx, cy):
            if (nx, ny) in visited:
                continue
            visited.add((nx, ny))
            if (nx, ny) in my_cells_set:
                return (cx, cy)
            if (nx, ny) in opp_cells_set:
                continue
            queue.append((nx, ny))
    return None

def find_reinforcement(cx, cy, my_cells, opp_cells):
    """An empty cell that is both adjacent to (cx, cy) and adjacent to our own
    territory (so it is a legal EXPAND target) - placing it raises our neighbor
    count around (cx, cy) by exactly one."""
    for nx, ny in neighbors(cx, cy):
        if (nx, ny) in my_cells or (nx, ny) in opp_cells:
            continue
        if any((mx, my_) in my_cells for mx, my_ in neighbors(nx, ny)):
            return (nx, ny)
    return None

def attack_setup_targets(my_cells, opp_cells):
    """Enemy cells adjacent to us where we are exactly one neighbor short of
    numerical superiority - reinforcing here turns a not-yet-legal ATTACK into a
    guaranteed one next turn, far cheaper than expanding blindly and hoping the
    numbers eventually favor us."""
    targets = []
    for ox, oy in opp_cells:
        if not any((nx, ny) in my_cells for nx, ny in neighbors(ox, oy)):
            continue
        my_n = count_neighbors(ox, oy, my_cells)
        opp_n = count_neighbors(ox, oy, opp_cells)
        if my_n == opp_n:
            reinforcement = find_reinforcement(ox, oy, my_cells, opp_cells)
            if reinforcement:
                targets.append(reinforcement)
    return targets

def cell_near_opponent(my_cells, opp_cells):
    """An empty cell adjacent to an opponent cell, picked closest to our own
    territory - the EXPAND fallback once local resources run out. An opponent's own
    cell is never a legal EXPAND destination, so aiming bfs_next_step directly at
    one degenerates the instant it's already adjacent (dist 1): the search returns
    that same occupied cell as the "step", which always fails the opp_cells check
    and is silently dropped - the bot sits on full energy right at the front line
    instead of claiming the real empty ground still available around the fight."""
    best, best_dist = None, None
    for ox, oy in opp_cells:
        for nx, ny in neighbors(ox, oy):
            if (nx, ny) in my_cells or (nx, ny) in opp_cells:
                continue
            d = min(max(abs(nx - cx), abs(ny - cy)) for cx, cy in my_cells)
            if best is None or d < best_dist:
                best, best_dist = (nx, ny), d
    return best

def vulnerable_cell_targets(my_cells, opp_cells):
    """Our own cells on the front line where the opponent already has (or is tied
    for) enough neighbors to ATTACK and take them - reinforcing denies them an
    easy, guaranteed capture."""
    targets = []
    for mx, my_ in my_cells:
        if not any((nx, ny) in opp_cells for nx, ny in neighbors(mx, my_)):
            continue
        my_n = count_neighbors(mx, my_, my_cells)
        opp_n = count_neighbors(mx, my_, opp_cells)
        if opp_n >= my_n:
            reinforcement = find_reinforcement(mx, my_, my_cells, opp_cells)
            if reinforcement:
                targets.append(reinforcement)
    return targets

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Game loop
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
while True:
    turn += 1
    parts = input().split()
    my_energy = int(parts[0])
    opp_energy = int(parts[1])

    # --- Read my cells ---
    my_cell_count = int(input())
    my_cells = set()
    for _ in range(my_cell_count):
        t = input().split()
        my_cells.add((int(t[0]), int(t[1])))

    # --- Read opponent cells ---
    opp_cell_count = int(input())
    opp_cells = set()
    for _ in range(opp_cell_count):
        t = input().split()
        opp_cells.add((int(t[0]), int(t[1])))

    # --- Read visible spots ---
    vis_spot_count = int(input())
    visible_spots = {}
    for _ in range(vis_spot_count):
        t = input().split()
        sx, sy, stype, rem = int(t[0]), int(t[1]), int(t[2]), int(t[3])
        visible_spots[(sx, sy)] = (stype, rem)
        known_spots[(sx, sy)] = (stype, rem)

    actions = []

    # --- Phase: Attack adjacent enemies with numerical superiority ---
    if opp_cells and my_energy >= 2:
        for ox, oy in sorted(opp_cells):
            if len(actions) >= 5 or my_energy < 2:
                break
            my_n = count_neighbors(ox, oy, my_cells)
            opp_n = count_neighbors(ox, oy, opp_cells)
            adj_to_mine = any((nx, ny) in my_cells for nx, ny in neighbors(ox, oy))
            if adj_to_mine and my_n > opp_n:
                actions.append(f"ATTACK {ox} {oy}")
                my_energy -= 2
                # Do not assume capture or reward; referee state arrives next turn.

    # --- Phase: Tactical reinforcement ---
    # A true full-depth search over "up to 5 actions across thousands of candidate
    # cells" is not viable inside the 50ms per-turn budget, so this is a cheap,
    # targeted heuristic instead of a game-tree search: look only at cells already
    # in contact (adjacent) with the enemy, where a single reinforcement either (a)
    # tips a near-miss ATTACK into a guaranteed one next turn, or (b) saves one of
    # our own front-line cells that the opponent could otherwise capture for free.
    # These are deliberately not gated by the economic energy-conservation throttle
    # below - by the time colonies are in contact, reaching a distant spot is
    # usually no longer the priority, and both actions are cheap, high-value, and
    # time-sensitive (the opponent may act on the same opportunity first). Budget of
    # 3 (not 2) reflects that a successful ATTACK is worth a flat scoring bonus on
    # top of its own per-turn territory value - tipping one more fight into a
    # guaranteed win next turn is worth crowding out slightly more expansion budget.
    placed = set()

    if opp_cells and len(actions) < 5 and my_energy >= 2:
        tactical_budget = min(3, 5 - len(actions))
        tactical_used = 0
        for target in attack_setup_targets(my_cells, opp_cells) + vulnerable_cell_targets(my_cells, opp_cells):
            if tactical_used >= tactical_budget or my_energy < 2:
                break
            if target in my_cells or target in opp_cells or target in placed:
                continue  # already reinforced by an earlier tactical target this turn
            actions.append(f"EXPAND {target[0]} {target[1]}")
            my_energy -= 2
            tactical_used += 1
            placed.add(target)

    # --- Phase: Expand ---
    # Reaching a spot can only ever advance by one hop per turn no matter how many
    # actions are spent that turn - same-turn EXPANDs cannot chain off each other,
    # so a second or third simultaneous "step" toward the very same target is pure
    # waste, not extra speed. The number of *extra* (non-critical-path) actions
    # affordable this turn scales gradually with surplus energy above what's needed
    # to secure the nearest spot: an all-or-nothing switch (spend wide the instant
    # any margin exists) blows the whole margin in a single wide turn - a lone
    # Small spot only pays +1/turn, nowhere near enough to refill that in one go -
    # and immediately drops back below the threshold, oscillating without ever
    # accumulating real surplus.
    undepleted = {pos: info for pos, info in known_spots.items() if info[1] > 0}

    def raw_distance(pos):
        return min(max(abs(pos[0] - cx), abs(pos[1] - cy)) for cx, cy in my_cells)

    # Oppression-aware priority (lower is better) - a pure "nearest empty ground"
    # scan treats every target as equally worth reaching, which wins territory but
    # not fights or resource denial. Two biases push toward winning by oppression
    # instead: a bigger spot is worth travelling a bit further for (it's more
    # resource, and resource the opponent doesn't get either), and a target nearer
    # the OPPONENT than to us is worth extra priority - claiming it both grows our
    # colony and starves theirs, rather than just safely expanding into our own
    # corner. This same function ranks resource spots and the opponent-contact
    # target side by side, so pursuing a fight can win out over one more spot
    # instead of always being the last resort.

            if opp_dist < dist:

        return dist - value_bonus - oppression_bonus

    # Where to head once there's nothing left to secure: the opponent's corner is
    # always known exactly (start positions are fixed), so once local spots run out
    # this pushes toward contesting territory / setting up ATTACK opportunities
    # instead of picking an arbitrary map-center point with no strategic value.
    opp_corner = (MAP_SIZE - 1, MAP_SIZE - 1) if MY_ID == 0 else (0, 0)

    undepleted_sorted = sorted(undepleted.keys(), key=target_priority) if undepleted else []
    opp_target = (cell_near_opponent(my_cells, opp_cells) if opp_cells else None) or opp_corner

    # The opponent-contact target competes on equal footing with every known spot
    # for BOTH the guaranteed baseline hop and the bonus actions below - not just as
    # a fallback once spots run dry - so a strong oppression opportunity can win the
    # baseline slot over one more (weaker) spot instead of always waiting its turn.

    # Always guarantee at least one directed hop per turn - whether still traveling
    # to the nearest spot or already parked on one. An earlier version withheld
    # this baseline entirely once parked (dist == 0), reasoning that spending
    # against a single spot's 1/turn income was a slow bleed with nothing banked
    # for the next journey; in practice that meant waiting for a large surplus to
    # accumulate before spending *anything*, so the bot sat idle for most of a
    # 300-turn game even with plenty of energy in hand. The bot no longer needs

    # fixed corner (never a dead end), BFS routes around enemy territory instead of
    # getting silently stuck on it, and the flat safety_margin below still keeps a
    # small buffer against exactly this kind of temporary net-negative spend.

    expand_budget = min(5 - len(actions), 1 + bonus_actions)
    expand_used = 0

    # Guaranteed critical-path hop toward the nearest spot (skip if already there).

        if step and step not in my_cells and step not in opp_cells and step not in placed:
            actions.append(f"EXPAND {step[0]} {step[1]}")
            my_energy -= 2

            placed.add(step)

    # Any remaining budget goes toward the next-closest known spots, one directed
    # hop each - not a generic "nearest frontier cell" scan, which tends to cluster
    # several actions on the same immediate neighborhood instead of making progress
    # toward multiple distinct targets. The opponent (visible cells, or their fixed
    # starting corner if not yet seen) is always in the mix too: a colony that has
    # secured its spots otherwise has no reason to ever move toward the enemy, and
    # ends up sitting on full energy instead of contesting territory or setting up
    # ATTACK opportunities, which require being adjacent to an enemy cell first.

    # single point (everything reachable from one owned cell funnels through the
    # same neighbor first) - without deduplicating against `placed`, this loop would

    # copy can ever succeed (same-turn snapshot, no chaining), so the rest just burn
    # energy for nothing - and because the very next turn's reserve is recalculated
    # from whatever energy is left, that wasted spend permanently erases the surplus
    # instead of carrying it forward, locking the bot into the 1-action/turn floor
    # for the rest of the game instead of ever affording a genuine multi-hop turn.

    # failed in different ways: picking the FEWEST-neighbor cell almost always

    # currently pursuing sidesteps colony shape entirely - it always finds a
    # candidate, and a distant cell can't be part of the active frontier or the path
    # we're relying on right now, so it can't reintroduce that oscillation either.

            my_cells.discard((cx, cy))
            my_energy += 1

    if not actions:
        actions.append("WAIT")

    print("; ".join(actions), flush=True)

The Goal

You control a bacterial colony on a Petri dish. Expand your territory, harvest nutrient spots for energy, and eliminate all enemy cells before the turn limit.
Score builds up turn by turn from territory held and fights won — not just a snapshot of the final board — so sustained control and successful attacks both compound over the whole game.
Inspired by Conway's Game of Life: cells occupy a grid and compete for space, but here each move is a deliberate, costed action rather than a fixed birth/death rule applied uniformly every step.

 Rules

▶ The Map

  • A 64 × 64 square grid. (0, 0) is top-left, x grows to the right, y grows downward.
  • Player 0 starts with one cell at (0, 0) (top-left).
  • Player 1 starts with one cell at (63, 63) (bottom-right).
  • Nutrient spots are placed symmetrically (180° rotation).
  • Two cells are adjacent if they are within one cell of each other, horizontally, vertically, or diagonally (up to 8 surrounding cells). This term is used throughout the statement for EXPAND placement and tie-breaks.
  • A cell's neighbors are the adjacent cells belonging to a given player. Neighbor counts are used to determine ATTACK numerical superiority and to break EXPAND ties.

▶ Nutrient Spots

Each spot has a type that determines its total energy reserve:

Type Code Total Energy
● Small 1 20
● Medium 2 60
● Large 3 140

If one of your cells occupies a nutrient spot, it automatically extracts 1 energy per turn until the spot is depleted.

▶ Energy

Starting energy is calculated as a function of the distance between your base and the nearest nutrient spot, plus a safety margin. Both players always start with the same amount of energy — the map's 180° symmetry guarantees it. Energy is spent to perform actions.

▶ Actions (up to 5 per turn)

Action Syntax Energy cost Effect
EXPAND EXPAND x y 2 Place a new cell at (x, y). The target must be empty and adjacent to one of your existing cells. If the placement is invalid, the energy cost is still spent (wasted move).
ATTACK ATTACK x y 2 Attack an enemy cell at (x, y). Succeeds if you have strictly more allied neighbors around the target than the defender has. On success: the enemy cell is destroyed, your cell takes its place, and you gain +4 energy. On failure: energy is still spent.
APOPTOSIS APOPTOSIS x y 0 Sacrifice one of your own cells at (x, y). Recovers +1 energy.
WAIT WAIT 0 Do nothing.

Combine multiple actions with ; — Example: EXPAND 1 0; EXPAND 0 1; WAIT

The referee first collects both players lines, then resolves by global action phase: EXPAND → ATTACK → APOPTOSIS → WAIT.

▶ Fog of War

  • The grid is split down the middle into two halves: columns x < 32 are Player 0's half, columns x ≥ 32 are Player 1's half — i.e. the half containing your starting corner.
  • You always see all nutrient spots on your half of the map.
  • Enemy cells and enemy-half spots are visible only within Chebyshev distance 5 of any of your cells.

You win if:

  • Knockout — you destroy all of your opponent's cells.
  • Turn limit (300 turns) — at the last turn, you have the higher accumulated score.
    Tiebreaker: total enemy cells destroyed during the game.
  • Your opponent loses (see Defeat Conditions below).

Score is not a final snapshot — it accumulates every turn: each turn, you bank 1 point per cell you currently own, so holding territory longer is always worth more than holding it briefly. A successful ATTACK also grants an immediate +300 bonus on top of that turn's accrual — roughly 60% of the winning score in a combat-heavy game comes from attack bonuses alone, making direct combat the single highest-value action available, well above passive expansion. Holding a majority of the map has no special threshold effect beyond this: it simply compounds into a bigger score lead the longer it's held, so both turtling behind a safe majority and contesting resources or attacking directly are viable paths to victory — but passivity is never rewarded on its own.

You lose if:

  • Knockout — all of your cells are destroyed.
  • Timeout — you don't output a line within the response time limit.
  • No output — your program exits or provides no output line for a turn.
  • Invalid output — your output line doesn't match the expected format (unknown action, wrong number of arguments, non-integer coordinates, or more than 5 actions).

Trying to EXPAND or ATTACK without enough energy is not a defeat condition — see Expert Rules for what happens instead.

 Expert Rules

  • The map has 180° rotational symmetry: every nutrient spot has a mirrored counterpart, which is why both players always start with equal energy.
  • Each turn, all players receive input and output is collected before any action is resolved. Resolution order is fixed by phase: EXPAND, then ATTACK, then APOPTOSIS, then WAIT.
  • An EXPAND or ATTACK you cannot afford is simply skipped: no energy is spent and it has no effect. This is different from an invalid or failed action (occupied target, no numerical superiority, etc.), which still costs energy — see below.
  • If you target the same cell with more than one EXPAND (or ATTACK) in the same turn, only the first one (in your output line's order) is evaluated; the rest still cost energy but have no effect.
  • If both players EXPAND into the same empty cell, the winner is the player with the highest neighbor count around that target (computed from the phase snapshot — the state of the grid at the start of the turn, before any of this turn's actions are applied). If still tied, lower player index wins. An EXPAND that loses this tie-break still costs energy, exactly like any other failed EXPAND.
  • EXPAND adjacency and occupancy are validated on the phase snapshot; chain-expanding from newly created cells in the same turn is not possible.
  • ATTACK majority is computed from the attack-phase snapshot — the state of the grid immediately after all EXPAND actions for the turn have been resolved — then successful captures are applied deterministically by target coordinate order.
  • A failed EXPAND (occupied or not adjacent) still costs energy.
  • A failed ATTACK (no numerical majority) still costs energy.
  • A failed APOPTOSIS (not your cell) costs nothing and gains nothing.
  • Passive nutrient extraction happens after all actions, once per turn.

Referee source code: github.com/Amatsukan/BacterI.A.

 Game Protocol

Initialization input

Line 1: two space-separated integers:

  • mapSize — grid side length (always 64)
  • myIndex — your player index (0 or 1)

Line 2: one integer spotCount — number of nutrient spots visible on your half.

Next spotCount lines: three space-separated integers per spot:

  • x, y — position of the spot
  • type — 1=Small, 2=Medium, 3=Large
Input per turn

Line 1: two space-separated integers myEnergy oppEnergy

  • myEnergy — your current energy
  • oppEnergy — your opponent's current energy

Line 2: one integer myCellCount — number of cells you own

Next myCellCount lines: two space-separated integers per cell:

  • x, y — coordinates of one of your cells

Next line: one integer oppCellCount — number of visible enemy cells

Next oppCellCount lines: two space-separated integers per cell:

  • x, y — coordinates of a visible enemy cell

Next line: one integer visibleSpotCount — number of visible nutrient spots this turn

Next visibleSpotCount lines: four space-separated integers per spot:

  • x, y — position of the spot
  • type — 1=Small, 2=Medium, 3=Large
  • remainingEnergy — energy left in the spot
Output

A single line with up to 5 actions separated by ;

Example: EXPAND 1 0; ATTACK 3 4; WAIT

Constraints
Grid size64 × 64
Max turns300
Response time per turn≤ 50 ms
First turn response time≤ 1000 ms

 Example Turn

Initialization input (Player 0):
Input line Meaning
64 0 mapSize=64, myIndex=0
1 spotCount=1 — one nutrient spot visible on your half
5 3 1 a Small spot at (5, 3)
Turn 1 input (Player 0):
Input line Meaning
25 25 myEnergy=25, oppEnergy=25
1 myCellCount=1
0 0 your only cell, at (0, 0)
0 oppCellCount=0 — no enemy cells visible yet
1 visibleSpotCount=1
5 3 1 20 a Small spot at (5, 3) with 20 energy remaining
Your output:
EXPAND 1 0; EXPAND 1 1

You spend 4 energy to place two new cells. Energy drops to 21.

Invalid action examples
  • EXPAND 10 10 on a non-adjacent cell: fails and still costs 2.
  • ATTACK 4 4 without numerical superiority: fails and still costs 2.
  • APOPTOSIS 4 4 on a cell you do not own: fails, no gain, no cost.
